questions.title: CK-MB isoenzyme is present mainly in heart muscle
questions.question: The creatine kinase MB (CK-MB) isoenzyme is present mainly in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Brain contains the CK-BB isoenzyme, not CK-MB.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Skeletal muscle contains mainly CK-MM, with little CK-MB.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The kidney is not the characteristic tissue for CK-MB.
explanations.D: Correct. Creatine kinase is a dimer of M and B subunits, and the MB isoenzyme is found mainly in cardiac muscle. A rise in serum CK-MB is therefore used as a marker of myocardial injury (e.g. acute myocardial infarction). Its tissue specificity is the point being tested.

questions.learning_objective: State that CK-MB is characteristic of cardiac muscle.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Heart Muscle", p179

questions.title: Cutting the sympathetic supply to the skin causes loss of sweating
questions.question: Cutting the sympathetic supply to the skin results in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cutting the nerve removes the drive to sweat, so sweating decreases, not increases.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Loss of sympathetic vasoconstrictor tone causes vasodilatation, not vasoconstriction.
explanations.C: Correct. Sweat glands are supplied by sympathetic fibres that are cholinergic (they release acetylcholine). Cutting this sympathetic supply removes the secretomotor drive, so the denervated skin loses its ability to sweat (anhidrosis). This is why the answer is loss of sweating despite the fibres being sympathetic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Salivary secretion is controlled by nerves to the salivary glands, not by the cutaneous sympathetic supply.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Piloerection is produced by sympathetic activation of arrector pili; cutting the sympathetic supply abolishes it rather than causing it.

questions.learning_objective: Explain loss of sweating after sympathetic denervation (cholinergic sympathetic fibres).
questions.subject: neuro

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Loss of sweating", p161

questions.title: Cutting the parasympathetic (vagal) supply to the thorax raises heart rate
questions.question: Cutting the parasympathetic supply to the thorax results in:

explanations.A: Correct. The vagus carries the parasympathetic supply to the thoracic viscera and continuously slows the heart. Cutting it removes vagal (parasympathetic) tone, so the sinoatrial node runs faster and the heart rate increases. This is the resting tachycardia of vagal denervation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Glycogenolysis is a metabolic effect of sympathetic/adrenaline action, not a result of thoracic vagal section.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Constipation would follow loss of parasympathetic supply to the gut (abdominal), and even then reduced motility; it is not the thoracic effect asked about.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pupillodilatation is an eye (head) effect of sympathetic activity or loss of parasympathetic input to the pupil, not of thoracic vagal section.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Most blood vessels have no parasympathetic supply, so cutting the thoracic parasympathetic does not cause generalised vasodilatation.

questions.learning_objective: State that loss of vagal tone increases heart rate.
questions.subject: neuro

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Increased heart rate", p163

questions.title: Sympathetic output to the bladder is noradrenergic
questions.question: You review the autonomic supply of various organs. Which of the following nervous outputs is noradrenergic?

explanations.A: Incorrect. All parasympathetic postganglionic fibres are cholinergic, so the parasympathetic supply to the heart is not noradrenergic.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The sympathetic fibres to sweat glands are a special exception: they are cholinergic, not noradrenergic.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Parasympathetic output to the bronchi is cholinergic.
explanations.D: Correct. Most sympathetic postganglionic fibres release noradrenaline (they are adrenergic); the sympathetic output to the bladder is one such noradrenergic fibre. This contrasts with the cholinergic exceptions (sweat glands) and the cholinergic adrenal-medulla supply. So the sympathetic supply to the bladder is the noradrenergic answer.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The adrenal medulla is innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibres, which are cholinergic (acting on nicotinic receptors), not noradrenergic.

questions.learning_objective: Identify sympathetic postganglionic fibres to the bladder as noradrenergic.
questions.subject: neuro

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Sympathetic output to the bladder", p164
